newsitem.title: GERMANY: MOTOR RACING-FRENTZEN GETS BOOST FROM BORUSSIA.
newsitem.headline: MOTOR RACING-FRENTZEN GETS BOOST FROM BORUSSIA.

text.p: Germany's under-fire Formula One racing driver Heinz-Harald Frentzen has received encouragement from an unexpected quarter -- his favourite soccer team.

Germany's SID sports news agency reported on Friday that Borussia Moenchengladbach captain Stefan Effenberg had sent a fax to Frentzen on behalf of the team telling him not to be downhearted about his performances so far with Williams.
"We've also had to cope with a lot of setbacks in the past," the former Germany midfielder's message read. "We know what you're capable of and we're all crossing our fingers for you."
Frentzen, who comes from Moenchengladbach, has failed to score a single point in his first three grands prix.

His soccer team suffered a similarly dismal start to their season, going into the Bundesliga's winter shut down in a relegation place. But they have staged a strong recovery in the second half of the season and now lie comfortably in mid-table.
The driver would be well advised to follow Effenberg's words rather than his actions when it comes to dealing with criticism.
The midfielder was sent home from the 1994 World Cup finals in the United States after making an obscene gesture at mocking German fans during a match.
